clue.text: Around back of kitchen, attack a pancake

indicators.note: placed around means one word wraps itself about the other letter
'back of' keeps only the last letter of 'kitchen'

blocks.note: a blitz is a sudden all-out attack
the final letter of kitchen

explanation.surface: A cook rushes round the back of the kitchen to tackle a pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: BLITZ goes around N, so the comma after kitchen hides that 'Around' governs the attack word.
explanation.definitionFit: A blintz is a thin rolled pancake from Jewish cooking, usually stuffed with cheese.

clue.text: Pursuing hit, let's recast fashionable vessel

indicators.note: recasting something reshapes it, so the letters are reformed in another order

blocks.note: to bat is to hit
taken as written, apostrophe ignored, ready to be rearranged
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: After a hit show, someone suggests remaking a stylish ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Pursuing puts the other pieces after BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleship is a large, heavily armoured warship, a vessel in the naval sense.

clue.text: Native's pension consumed

blocks.note: a pension is a European boarding house or small hotel
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: An Indigenous person's retirement income has all been used up.
explanation.walkthrough: Pension is not retirement pay but the French word for a guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Native in the sense of inborn, as in native wit, means the same as innate.

clue.text: 1960s art seen in that component of a formal outfit

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: op art is the optical-illusion style of the 1960s
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sixties art appears on part of a dress suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Another of Monopoly's classic tokens.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is the tall silk hat worn with white tie or morning dress.

clue.text: Portal opened wide, nearly revolving with effort

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
something revolving turns around, so the letters run the other way
with here means holding, so one piece is carried inside the other

blocks.note: to yawn is to open the mouth wide
a try is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: A doorway swung wide open, almost spinning, after a hard push.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opened wide' sounds like the door itself, but it describes a mouth; the portal is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An entryway is the passage or door by which you go in, a synonym of portal.

clue.text: Neon Speedo, oddly, is detected by 24

indicators.note: oddly means at the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third, fifth letters are kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A bright swimsuit is noticed by smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is SMELL, at 24 down. Speedo is a brand of swimwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose something out is to detect it by scent, so nosed means found by smell.

clue.text: It goes fast, whether heading north or south

indicators.note: in a down entry, north is up and south is down, so the word reads the same in both directions

blocks.note: the surface reading: a quick vehicle
the setter's reading: the letters read the same up or down the grid

explanation.surface: A speedy vehicle, whichever direction it drives.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelt as one word, as Americans write it, so it is a true palindrome; another Monopoly token.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecar is a car built for speed competitions, so it is something that goes fast.

clue.text: This is a lot of fun: pound a projectile implement for hauling

blocks.clueFragment: This is a lot of fun
blocks.note: whee is what you shout when enjoying yourself
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
an arrow is a projectile shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Pounding away with a missile tool is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase is not commentary but the exclamation itself; another Monopoly token.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelbarrow is a one-wheeled cart pushed by hand for carrying loads such as soil.

clue.text: Timeless toy coming up repeatedly!

indicators.note: without time means the letter standing for time is removed
in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom
repeatedly means said more than once, so the piece is written twice

blocks.note: taken as written
the same word again, as repeatedly asks

explanation.surface: A classic plaything keeps springing back up.
explanation.walkthrough: T is time; it is dropped, the rest read upwards, then doubled. The whole clue also describes a yo-yo climbing its string again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a spool toy that climbs its string repeatedly, and it has been popular for generations.

clue.text: Money spent unwisely on overtime

indicators.note: something done unwisely is done badly, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
OT is the standard abbreviation for overtime in US sports and pay slips

explanation.surface: Cash from extra hours is wasted foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money spent unwisely' reads as a phrase, but only Money is the definition; spent is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-spot is American slang for a ten-dollar bill, so it is a sum of money.

clue.text: Story involving stray dog

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a tier is a storey or level of a building
to err is to stray from what is right

explanation.surface: A tale about a lost dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Story is a tale on the surface but a building level here, spelt the American way. The Scottie dog Monopoly token is a terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed type of small, lively dog, such as the Scottish terrier.

clue.text: After a short time, cry uncontrollably about launch of evil policy the CIA depends on

indicators.note: something out of control runs wild, so the letters are scrambled
about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round another

blocks.note: SEC is short for a second
taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the launch of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sobs wildly over an evil scheme the spy agency relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: An intelligence agency depends on keeping its doings hidden, and secrecy is that concealment, so the definition is descriptive.

clue.text: Carly improved synthetic fiber

indicators.note: improving something reworks it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the name taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman called Carly makes a better artificial thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the trade name of spandex, a stretchy man-made fibre used in sportswear.

clue.text: Reptile's accordion playing captivates Long Island

definitions.note: possessive standing for an adjective: of or belonging to the crocodile family

indicators.note: an instrument being played is worked about, so the letters are rearranged
captivates means holds captive, so the other letters are kept inside

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
LI is the standard abbreviation for Long Island, New York

explanation.surface: An alligator squeezes an accordion and wows Long Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reptile's' reads as a possessive noun; the answer is the adjective it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodilian describes crocodiles, alligators and their relatives, the reptile order Crocodilia.

clue.text: Mock authority imprisoning myself with Cheney endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
imprisoning means locking inside, so the outer word holds the others

blocks.note: rule is power or authority
the speaker refers to self as I
Dick Cheney, US vice president under George W. Bush

explanation.surface: A satirical swipe at power that jails the speaker alongside Dick Cheney.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheney contributes his first name, Dick, not his surname; he was vice president under George W. Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to ridicule them, holding them up to scornful laughter.

clue.text: Vile nastiness engulfing a French composer

indicators.note: something vile is corrupted, so the letters are spoiled into a new order
engulfing means swallowing up, so one letter goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French composer swallowed up by foul spite.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give S INTSAENS, with A dropped in after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Saint-Saens was a French Romantic composer, known for The Carnival of the Animals.

clue.text: Small tool to make part of a brake

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a hoe is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A little implement is needed to build a piece of a braking system.
explanation.walkthrough: It is also one of the classic Monopoly tokens, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake shoe is the curved block that presses against a wheel drum to slow it.

clue.text: Nineteenth-century artifacts, collected initially in haphazard variation

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken
haphazard means in random order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the opening letter of collected
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Old objects from the 1800s gathered in a random assortment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' seems to describe the artifacts as a collection, but it only lends one letter to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoriana are objects made during Queen Victoria's reign, 1837 to 1901, valued now as collectables.

clue.text: Opening above a door extended inside the majority of building

indicators.note: building means putting together, so the letters are assembled in a new order
inside means placed within the other piece

blocks.note: most means the greater part, the majority
ran means extended, as a road runs to the coast

explanation.surface: A gap over a doorway reaching into most of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the majority of building' looks like a part of a building, but the majority is a word of its own and building tells you to reassemble it.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is the small hinged window over a door, called a fanlight in Britain.

clue.text: Lives with different man, almost exactly as hot

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: is means exists or lives
other means different
a man is a male

explanation.surface: Someone shacks up with a new partner who is nearly as attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as hot' suggests attractiveness, but here hot is literal temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Isothermal describes places or processes at a constant, equal temperature.

clue.text: One type of jazz instrument keeps decibels at zero

indicators.note: keeps means holds onto, so the outer word contains the others

blocks.note: a harp is a stringed instrument
dB is the symbol for decibels
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: A jazz instrument turns the volume right down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jazz instrument' reads as a phrase, but the definition ends at jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard bop is a 1950s jazz style that grew out of bebop, adding blues and gospel.

clue.text: Reversed sushi ingredient's decrease?

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: nori is the seaweed wrapped around sushi rolls

explanation.surface: A sushi chef asks whether a backward ingredient means less of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read decrease as de-crease: an iron takes creases out. The question mark flags the pun, and it is another Monopoly token.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron cloth is to remove its creases, so the punning 'de-crease' describes it.

clue.text: Game of chance after sip of beverage is drunk

indicators.note: a sip takes only a little from the start, so just the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of beverage
lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: After a sip of a drink, a lottery player is intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the game after the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is informal slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Jerk in retreat dodges grapefruit, lemons, and oranges

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
dodges are tricks or ruses

explanation.surface: A retreating fool ducks flying fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: TIC runs backwards to CIT. Jerk and dodges look like actions, but both are nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapefruit, lemons and oranges are all examples of citrus fruits, so together they are citruses.

clue.text: Odor from dump overwhelming mayor at first

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is wanted
overwhelming means engulfing, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: to dump shares or goods is to sell them off cheaply
the opening letter of mayor

explanation.surface: A stench from the tip overpowers the mayor.
explanation.walkthrough: Dump looks like a noun, a rubbish heap, but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell is an odour, especially an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Lots of grass in Oregon, ultimately breaking ordinances

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is wanted
breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: ordinances are laws
the final letter of Oregon

explanation.surface: Plenty of marijuana in Oregon is against local regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass hints at marijuana, legal in Oregon, but the definition means turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawns are plots of mown grass, so 'lots' here are pieces of land rather than a quantity.

clue.text: Time edited article

indicators.note: edited means revised, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A magazine piece that was revised.
explanation.walkthrough: Time looks like the news magazine; it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is an individual thing, or a piece in a newspaper, just as an article is.

clue.text: Protection for a finger that some might say is a thign?

indicators.note: some speakers, those with a lisp, pronounce the word differently, so it is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a symbol is a sign, and the misspelling thign shows a lisper turning s into th

explanation.surface: A finger guard that a lisping speaker might call a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thign' is no typo: it is 'sign' with a lisp, and a lisped 'symbol' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble is the small metal cap worn on a fingertip to push a needle while sewing.

clue.text: How Macbeth introduces himself to Tarzan? That's a gas!

blocks.clueFragment: How Macbeth introduces himself to Tarzan
blocks.note: Tarzan's famous greeting is 'Me Tarzan'

explanation.surface: A joke about Shakespeare's Scottish lord meeting the jungle hero, ending 'That's a gas!' as in hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth is Thane of Cawdor; a thane is a Scottish lord. 'A gas' also means a hoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the colourless flammable gas that is the main component of natural gas.

clue.text: See 2
Low, deceptive ploy to capture knight in a game you could play with one of the eight classic 31 in the grid

definitions.text: a game you could play with one of the eight classic 31 in the grid

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so one word holds the other
something deceptive misleads by its appearance, so the letters are disguised in a new order

blocks.note: to low is to moo, like a cow
N is the chess notation for a knight
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sly trick to take a chess knight, in a game using classic playing pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside MOO; the 31 are the TOKENS in the last across, and the theme answers are Monopoly's eight classic tokens.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopoly is the property-trading board game whose players move metal tokens such as the top hat and iron.

clue.text: Rolling Stone includes $1,000 souvenirs

indicators.note: something rolling tumbles over, so the letters are mixed up
includes means holds within, so one letter is put inside

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stones member keeps expensive memorabilia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' reads as the band or the magazine, but Rolling is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A token can be a keepsake or memento, kept as a reminder of an event.
